PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-07-27
60M, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. He reports two months of episodic wheezing and chest tightness, mostly on cold mornings and after climbing stairs, easing within several minutes of rest. Denies chest pain. He completed surveillance colonoscopy last year and was told it was clear; bowel habits are regular. He works as a delivery driver with long stretches of sitting and irregular meals. Family has noticed alternating periods of elevated, high-energy mood and low mood over recent months, which he is willing to explore. Diet is high in sugary drinks, which was discussed. Lives with his spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 126/78, HR 74, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 198 lb, BMI 29.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: nasal mucosa normal, oropharynx clear.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally at rest today.
Abdomen: well-healed surgical scar, soft, nontender.
Psych: cooperative, normal speech rate today, linear thought process.
Labs (prior week): Hgb 12.1 g/dL, A1c 6.1%, glucose 106 mg/dL fasting.

A/P:
1. Possible mild intermittent asthma; will trial albuterol. Albuterol inhaler 2 puffs before exertion or as needed for wheezing. Inhaler technique reviewed. Spirometry ordered.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding short walks during breaks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
3. Anemia, stable on recheck. Continue oral iron every other day. Repeat CBC in 3 months.
4. Concern for bipolar disorder; referred to psychiatry. Provided referral and reviewed warning signs to seek earlier care.
5. History of colon cancer, s/p resection in 2022. Continue colorectal screening per the gastroenterology schedule.

Return in 6 weeks to review spirometry, sooner if breathing worsens.
